## ✨ Added
- **`ENABLE_REGISTRATION`** (default `false`). When `true`, open self-service signup is enabled and Element shows its **Create Account** button (`UIFeature.registration`). It stays off by default: only enable it behind a CAPTCHA or on a trusted network, or you will get spam signups. (Synapse refuses to start with open registration and no verification, so the container also sets `enable_registration_without_verification` to match the toggle.)
- **`TURN_DOMAIN`** (default: `SERVER_NAME`) and **`TURN_PORT`** (default `3478`). Route TURN (voice/video) through a dedicated subdomain and/or a remapped port, for example to take coturn around a reverse proxy. The `turn_uris` Synapse advertises now follow these instead of being hard-coded to `SERVER_NAME:3478`.

## ⚡ Improved
- README section 6 (Enabling Federation) rewritten: no manual `.well-known` proxy locations are needed anymore.

## 🐛 Fixed
- **Federation discovery now works out of the box.** The image previously claimed to serve `/.well-known/matrix/server` and `/.well-known/matrix/client` on port 8080, but nothing actually served them, so federation returned 404 unless you hand-wrote the JSON in your reverse proxy. Synapse now serves both itself via `serve_server_wellknown` + `public_baseurl`, delegating incoming federation to port **443**, so as long as `https://SERVER_NAME/` is routed to Synapse (the standard reverse-proxy setup), federation works with **no extra proxy rules**. Any manual `/.well-known/matrix/*` locations can be removed.
Resolves #5, thanks to @i-byrana for the detailed report and the suggested fixes.
- **`ADMIN_USER` now promotes an *existing* account to server admin.** The admin bootstrap only set the server-admin flag when it *created* the account (`register_new_matrix_user -a`); if the account already existed, for example one you registered in Element first, it was left as a normal user. Synapse-Admin needs a Synapse **server admin** (not the same as an Element *room* admin), so it loaded but every data request failed with **"Server communication error"** (the `/_synapse/admin` API returns 403). The bootstrap now promotes the existing account directly in PostgreSQL (the documented way to grant server admin): set `ADMIN_USER`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD` to that account and restart. It only sets the admin flag; it does not change the password. Init also no longer skips the admin step when an earlier run left a marker file, so re-setting `ADMIN_USER` on an existing install is enough to promote. Fail-safe: it retries on the next restart if Postgres isn't reachable yet. Thanks to the reporter in #6.
